The '''Imperial Cult''' was the official state religion and political-religious institution of the [[Vesperan Empire]]. It presented the [[Emperor of Vespera]] as the earthly representative of divine order and made loyalty to the emperor both a civic and religious obligation.

== Doctrine ==

The cult's central doctrine was imperial divine mandate. The emperor was treated as the highest point of the social, political, and religious order, while obedience to imperial authority was framed as service to the stability of the empire.

The cult reinforced hierarchy, military service, public loyalty, and the idea that Vespera united many peoples under one divinely sanctioned imperial system.

== Institutions ==

The cult was centered on the [[Great Temple of Vespera]] in the imperial capital. Religious officials, priests, and scholars were trained through the [[Imperial Religious Academy]], while senior religious figures advised the emperor and the [[Imperial Council]] on ritual, education, legitimacy, and cultural integration.

The cult's priesthood also helped imperial administrations in occupied and client territories translate local religious practice into forms acceptable to Vesperan rule.

== Local Faiths ==

The Imperial Cult did not require every subject to abandon local private religion. Instead, it demanded public recognition of the emperor's divine status and participation in imperial rites. Local faiths were tolerated when they did not challenge imperial authority.

This controlled pluralism helped the empire absorb conquered regions, but it also made religion a tool of political control.

== Collapse ==

The cult lost its status as a functioning state institution when the [[Vesperan Empire]] collapsed in 1949. The destruction of the Great Temple during the [[Avant Great War]] became one of the clearest symbols of the end of the imperial order.
